title: Equatorial Guinea turns stranded gas into a regional hub strategy | Wood Mackenzie
gist: As Alba declines, Equatorial Guinea wants to turn Punta Europa into a Gulf of Guinea gas and LNG hub. Confirmed phases deliver about 1 tcf, so success hinges on Yoyo-Yolanda, Ebano (about 3 tcf), Cameroon gas and a still-unfinanced Nigerian pipeline of up to 2,700 mmcfd.

insights.claim: Equatorial Guinea's gas story has centred on the Alba gas-condensate field for almost 30 years, but Alba is in late life, so the strategic question has shifted from managing decline to repositioning Punta Europa as a regional gas-processing and LNG hub.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Legacy-field decline is forcing EG to chase third-party feed gas to keep its LNG asset relevant.

insights.claim: The Gas Mega Hub uses existing infrastructure to commercialise gas that might otherwise stay stranded; Chevron's Alen tieback started in 2021, Alba infill drilling in 2025, and Aseng was sanctioned in April 2026.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Brownfield tiebacks are the low-capex route to extending LNG plant life.

insights.claim: Alen and Alba supply about 175 mmcfd of feed gas, rising to over 300 mmcfd once the single-well Aseng tieback in Block I starts; the three phases should commercialise about 1 tcf over the next decade.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Roughly 1 tcf over a decade is modest relative to plant capacity.

insights.claim: Even at full capacity the confirmed Gas Mega Hub phases fall short of EG LNG's liquefaction capacity, and the gap widens as they mature, so Punta Europa needs additional gas before Alba's remaining output runs out.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Under-utilisation risk at EG LNG raises the value of any new feed gas source.

insights.claim: Chevron's cross-border Yoyo-Yolanda project, unitised with Cameroon in February 2026, could deliver up to 350 mmcfd via a subsea tieback to Alen, with first gas targeted for late 2029.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: The largest identifiable near-term backfill, but not before late 2029.

insights.claim: Smaller Equatorial Guinean discoveries across Alba and Blocks D, O, EG-23, EG-31 and EG-08 add nearly 2 tcf of potential backfill, much of it close to existing pipelines.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Cheap, near-infrastructure volumes could roughly double the hub's commercialised gas versus the confirmed 1 tcf.

insights.claim: Block EG-27, renamed Ebano, holds around 3 tcf of contingent resources and could support a second LNG train at Punta Europa, if a hub-led development can outcompete a standalone FLNG option.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: The key swing asset deciding whether Punta Europa expands or just fills spare capacity.

insights.claim: Ebano's financing risk is real: it lies about 140 km from existing infrastructure, and the earlier Fortuna FLNG scheme collapsed in 2019 after failing to secure financing.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Distance and the Fortuna precedent weigh on bankability.

insights.claim: SONAGAS now owns Ebano outright, while ConocoPhillips has signed a Heads of Agreement to participate.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: A major entering signals developer interest in the block.

insights.claim: Cameroon has more than 6 tcf of largely stranded gas, and the end of the Hilli Episeyo FLNG contract in July 2026 has intensified its need for a new outlet.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Cameroonian supply is looking for a route to market, which favours Punta Europa pipeline linkage.

insights.claim: Etinde and the neighbouring Sapele discovery in Cameroon could realistically supply Punta Europa by pipeline.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Cross-border Cameroon gas is the most plausible mid-size hub feed.

insights.claim: The proposed Gulf of Guinea Gas Pipeline, backed by a 2024 bilateral treaty, would carry up to 2,700 mmcfd, roughly four times EG LNG's current capacity, enough to support domestic power, industrial feedstock and additional liquefaction trains.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: The only option that transforms Punta Europa from backfill into a true regional hub.
insights.locator: Nigeria offers the most transformative option

insights.claim: The Nigerian pipeline vision depends on firm gas commitments, bankable cross-border agreements and financing that has yet to emerge.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Treat the 2,700 mmcfd scale as optionality, not a base case.

insights.claim: Every route forward needs competitive commercial terms, committed upstream partners and confidence that Punta Europa can attract capital against FLNG and other global LNG options.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: Hub-versus-FLNG competition for capital is the central execution risk.

insights.claim: Equatorial Guinea's infrastructure, location and two decades of operating experience are advantages hard to replicate in the Gulf of Guinea, but the opportunity will narrow as Alba's legacy production declines.
insights.speaker: Tra Ho
insights.so_what: The decision window is time-limited, tied to Alba's decline curve.
